div.head: I Cn 18a
div.ab: Forþam ealle we sceolon ænne timan gebidan, þonne us wære leofre þonne eall þæt on middanearde is, þær we á worhtan þa hwile, þe we mihton, georne Godes willan.
Forðam ealle we sceolan ænne timan gebidan, þæt us wære leofra ðonne [all] þæt on middanearde is, ðær we aworhton ða hwile, ðe we mihton, georne Godes willan.
Forðam ealle we sculon anne timan gebydan, þonne us ware leofre þonn eall þæt on middanearde is, þæt we aworhton þa hwile, þe we mihton, georne Godes willan.
quia singulos nos tempus expectat, quo nobis esset carius, quam quicquid in orbe terrarum mundus obtinuit, Dei nostri uoluntatem fecisse, dum licuit.
quoniam omnis nostrum unum tempus uidebit, quando magis diligeret uoluntatem Dei fecisse quam [quidquid] in mundo habetur.
Forðam ealle we sceolan ænne timan gebidan, þæt us wære leofra ðonne all þæt on middanearde is, ðæ[t] we aworhton, ða hwile ðe we mihton, georne Godes willan.
Forþam ealle we sceolon ænne timan gebidan þonne us wære leofre þonne eall þæt on middanearde is, þæt we aworhtan, þa hwile þe we mihton, georne Godes willan.

Denn wir alle werden Einen Zeitpunkt erleben, da uns lieber denn alles was auf Erden ist [das] sein würde, dass (vorher? hätten dort G) wir Gottes Willen die Zeitdauer über, da wir konnten, eifrig (stets G) gethan hätten.
For we shall all live to see a time when it would be dearer to us than everything on earth that (before? had there, G) we had eagerly (always, G) done God's will while we could.
For we shall all arrive at a time when we shall wish, above all else in the world, that we had zealously done the will of God, as long as we could.
For we all will reach a point when we will wish more than anything in the world that we had readily carried out God’s will as long as we could.
div.note: G's ‘þær we á worhtan’ (A, Ld ‘þæt’); Liebermann would perhaps correct to ‘þæt ær’, as in 18.2 in A. Liebermann compares Wulfstan p. 113.; Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 299, October 2026 (MS Cons)

note.seg: ꝥ A Ld; þær we á worhtan Homileten nach Wulfstan 118. 208; schwankend þær und þæt Wulfstan 113; bessere vielleicht [laut ær in 18b] ꝥ ær, wie 18, 2 in A ꝥ is für þis
ꝥ A Ld; þær we á worhtan in the homilists after Wulfstan 118. 208; Wulfstan 113 wavers between þær and þæt; perhaps read [in view of ær in 18b] ꝥ ær, as in 18, 2 A has ꝥ is for þis

u. II 68: ‘wo uns am liebsten’ = im Himmel. Vgl. ‘dann wird ihm lieber sein als diese ganze lichte Schöpfung, wenn er [fromm gelebt hätte]’ Agsä. Gedicht Salomo 30.—Wulfstan sagt kräftiger: ‘lieber als was wir auf Erden hinterlassen’.

Below II 68: ‘where [it is] dearest to us’ = in heaven. Cf. ‘then it will be dearer to him than all this bright creation, if he [had lived piously]’, A.-S. poem Salomo 30.—Wulfstan puts it more forcefully: ‘dearer than what we leave behind on earth’.
Der Nom. c. infin. beider Lateiner geht auf þæt zurück.—Vgl. Einl. 9; Gl Jüngstes Gericht 2
The nom. c. infin. of both Latin translators goes back to þæt.—Cf. Introduction 9; Gl Jüngstes Gericht 2
